original_test_intent: Physically hot-swap the approved E1.S drive in its named bay and prove that the intended device re-enumerates with acceptable storage, PCIe and data-integrity state.
original_method: A qualified ESD-safe operator maps the drive serial to bay and OS/controller path, drains and protects data, performs the vendor-approved hot removal/insertion sequence, while the agent captures read-only pre/during/post storage and PCIe evidence; any DC cycle is a separately approved recovery step, not a substitute.
manual_activity: A qualified operator confirms the labeled E1.S bay and drive serial, removes and reinserts it under the approved live-service procedure, records physical evidence and leaves workloads stopped until explicit enumeration and health are verified.
required_inputs: Exact E1.S drive serial/PN/FW, bay, backplane, PCI BDF/controller and OS/NVMe path
Platform confirmation that the bay and drive support live hot swap in the selected power state
Vendor removal/insertion, dwell, latch, LED and ESD procedure
Workload drain, filesystem unmount/freeze, RAID/volume policy and backup/data-disposition approval
Expected disappearance/reappearance timing and stable identity after insertion
Enumeration, NVMe health, SMART, PCIe/AER/DPC, RAID/filesystem and event acceptance limits
Decision whether a DC cycle is required recovery, optional post-check or copied unrelated command
Independent BMC/console and storage recovery/rebuild plan
safety_requirements: Never infer the target from /dev naming; bind serial, bay and controller before removal
Do not remove boot, mounted, swap, RAID-member, LVM/device-mapper or active-write storage without explicit approved handling
Do not treat power off/on as execution of a hot-swap test
Use ESD and latch/service controls and stop on resistance, wrong bay or physical damage
Preserve kernel/BMC/storage evidence; do not clear logs
Stop on missing/wrong identity, AER/DPC, NVMe reset storm, RAID degradation, filesystem/data error, thermal/power anomaly or failed recovery; no automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Verify exact source variant and drive/bay/path identity
Collect read-only block/NVMe/PCIe/mount/RAID/volume/health baselines and event timeline
Guide operator checkpoints and correlate physical timestamps with disappearance/re-enumeration
Collect post-insertion identity/health and restoration evidence
Perform no physical handling, unmount/write, power cycle, reset, rebuild, retry or verdict without approval
engineer_actions: Resolve hot-swap sequence and whether DC cycle has any role
Approve exact target, data protection, service state and physical procedure
Review physical plus storage evidence and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Not fit for SD.1: it power-cycles the chassis and checks uptime/AER only. It neither performs the required physical hot swap nor proves the correct drive re-enumerated, and its shared-code note exposes cross-variant contamination.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use secure read-only identity/enumeration/health collection around the operator's approved live hot swap; keep any DC cycle as an explicitly authorized recovery/post-check step only.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: E1.S hot swap, re-enumeration criterion, Manual Validation and 60/60-minute estimates remain.

modernized_recommendation.status: HYBRID CRITICAL E1.S HOT-SWAP REVIEW WITH VARIANT AND DRIVE-IDENTITY INTERLOCKS
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind physical bay/serial to controller/BDF/NVMe identity, preserve a synchronized removal/reinsertion and OS event timeline, verify the same intended drive and acceptable storage stack return before workload restore.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds explicit identity, data protection, live-service authorization, enumeration/health criteria and recovery while rejecting the unrelated generic reboot command.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A DC reboot can prove only post-boot discovery; it cannot cover live disappearance, insertion detection, hot-plug control path or operator handling. Uptime and an AER tail cannot prove device identity or data integrity.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Linux device names can change after reinsertion, and multipath/RAID may keep a logical volume visible while the physical member is absent. Serial/BDF/bay correlation and stack-level health are required to avoid falsely accepting the wrong or degraded device.

project_override_considerations: If this platform does not support live E1.S service, engineering must retain the source hot-swap coverage as BLOCKED or explicitly revision-scoped N/A; replacing it with cold boot or the shared SY reboot variant is a coverage regression.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash plus all duplicate-code variant identities
Approved drive serial/bay/backplane/controller/BDF/path map and hot-swap procedure
Timestamped physical removal/reinsertion/latch/LED evidence and device disappearance/reappearance
Pre/post NVMe identity/health, PCIe/AER/DPC, kernel/BMC events, RAID/volume/filesystem state and restored workload authorization
DC-cycle disposition, no-wrong-drive/no-shared-variant/no-auto-retry audit, hashes and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master row requires physical E1.S hot swap and re-enumeration, but the matching DeepSeek command performs only a DC chassis cycle and cites unrelated shared SY.4/SY.5 reboot rows. That command cannot satisfy this variant's procedure or criteria.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The E1.S hot-swap purpose is clear and can be executed as a hybrid case after exact target, physical procedure and data/recovery approvals. The mismatched command is preserved for correction rather than making the review itself indeterminate.

engineering_decision_pending: Resolve Functionality row 1920 variant 7c72f0f9a6dbd8e3 of shared code Wistron-GB NV PVP HW-00465-V003: define the exact E1.S live hot-swap sequence and target mapping, and decide whether the supplied DC cycle is an optional recovery/post-check or copied unrelated SY.4/SY.5 behavior; provide enumeration/health/data-integrity criteria while preserving Master.
review_improvement: Restores exact shared-code variant identity, rejects the generic reboot substitution and adds safe physical/storage evidence needed to prove genuine E1.S hot-swap coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: Hot-swap acceptance has two independent identities: the physical bay/serial and the software path/controller that disappears and returns. A chassis reboot can re-enumerate a drive without ever exercising live removal detection, while RAID or multipath can mask an absent member. Only a synchronized physical and stack-level timeline proves the intended E1.S path was hot-serviced and restored without hidden degradation.
